pubcol-w-5d4b0916fd29964e.definition_en: to express great admiration or respect for someone's achievement
collocations: really take my hat off to
have to take my hat off
take my hat off to them
pubcol-w-5d4b0916fd29964e.example_simple: I take my hat off to her for finishing the marathon.
pubcol-w-5d4b0916fd29964e.example_complex: You have to take your hat off to a team that rebuilt the whole system in just three weeks.
pubcol-w-5d4b0916fd29964e.vi_meaning_correction: ngưỡng mộ, khâm phục ai đó

pubcol-w-3b2484e652f11aee.definition_en: to write down important points so you can remember them later
pubcol-w-3b2484e652f11aee.example_simple: I always take notes during the lesson.
pubcol-w-3b2484e652f11aee.example_complex: Taking notes in your own words helps you understand and remember the material far better.

pubcol-w-54a7801b76070184.definition_en: to write down information in short form to keep a record of it
pubcol-w-54a7801b76070184.example_simple: She took notes and wrote down the phone number quickly.
pubcol-w-54a7801b76070184.example_complex: As the speaker talked, I took notes, writing down only the ideas I might forget later.

pubcol-w-6bd163d94ceca500.definition_en: to pay attention to someone or something
pubcol-w-6bd163d94ceca500.example_simple: Please take notice of the signs at the entrance.
pubcol-w-6bd163d94ceca500.example_complex: Employers soon began to take notice of her consistently excellent results.

pubcol-w-e6baac54fa0c1b06.definition_en: to feel hurt or insulted by something someone says or does
pubcol-w-e6baac54fa0c1b06.example_simple: Don't take offence, but I think you're wrong.
pubcol-w-e6baac54fa0c1b06.example_complex: He tends to take offence at the mildest criticism, which makes feedback difficult.
pubcol-w-e6baac54fa0c1b06.vi_meaning_correction: phật ý, cảm thấy bị xúc phạm

pubcol-w-2041aa7008635d24.definition_en: to remove something from a place, or to take someone out somewhere
pubcol-w-2041aa7008635d24.example_simple: Can you take out the trash before you leave?
pubcol-w-2041aa7008635d24.example_complex: She took out her notebook and began writing down everything the doctor said.

pubcol-w-0831dad1f79980ae.definition_en: to buy an insurance policy to protect against loss or damage to something
collocations: take out insurance on the house
take out insurance on your car
pubcol-w-0831dad1f79980ae.example_simple: They took out insurance on their new home.
pubcol-w-0831dad1f79980ae.example_complex: Before shipping the artwork abroad, the gallery took out insurance on every piece in the collection.
pubcol-w-0831dad1f79980ae.vi_meaning_correction: mua bảo hiểm cho (thứ gì đó)

pubcol-w-8348c413705a6c63.definition_en: to borrow money from a bank or lender, usually to be repaid over time
pubcol-w-8348c413705a6c63.example_simple: They took out a loan to buy a car.
pubcol-w-8348c413705a6c63.example_complex: Many students have to take out a loan to cover the rising cost of university tuition.

pubcol-w-484d8f4b7815d176.definition_en: to be involved in an activity or event together with others
pubcol-w-484d8f4b7815d176.example_simple: Everyone can take part in the game.
pubcol-w-484d8f4b7815d176.example_complex: Thousands of volunteers took part in the clean-up campaign across the city.

pubcol-w-19e57fb7f44822d2.definition_en: to happen, especially as a planned event
pubcol-w-19e57fb7f44822d2.example_simple: The wedding will take place on Saturday.
pubcol-w-19e57fb7f44822d2.example_complex: The negotiations took place behind closed doors, so few details were made public.

pubcol-w-25ef114e948bc556.definition_en: to happen or occur, usually as a scheduled or arranged event
pubcol-w-25ef114e948bc556.example_simple: The meeting took place in the main hall.
pubcol-w-25ef114e948bc556.example_complex: The festival takes place every autumn and draws visitors from around the world.

pubcol-w-db92934c12b68579.definition_en: to be treated as more important than something else
pubcol-w-db92934c12b68579.example_simple: My family takes priority over work.
pubcol-w-db92934c12b68579.example_complex: In an emergency, patient safety must take priority over all other concerns.

pubcol-w-c6e2c5d42c96db0d.definition_en: to be extremely successful very quickly and win the admiration of people
pubcol-w-c6e2c5d42c96db0d.example_simple: The new band took the country by storm.
pubcol-w-c6e2c5d42c96db0d.example_complex: Her debut novel took the literary world by storm, selling a million copies within months.
pubcol-w-c6e2c5d42c96db0d.vi_meaning_correction: gây tiếng vang lớn, chinh phục nhanh chóng

pubcol-w-0762983fbcd5bc73.definition_en: to happen unexpectedly so that someone is not prepared
collocations: the news took me by surprise
pubcol-w-0762983fbcd5bc73.example_simple: The sudden rain took us by surprise.
pubcol-w-0762983fbcd5bc73.example_complex: The announcement took the whole department by surprise, as no one had expected such a change.
pubcol-w-0762983fbcd5bc73.vi_meaning_correction: làm ai đó ngạc nhiên, bất ngờ

pubcol-w-0803214e730b73d5.definition_en: to deceive or cheat someone, often for money
pubcol-w-0803214e730b73d5.example_simple: The salesman took them for a ride.
pubcol-w-0803214e730b73d5.example_complex: By the time she realised the investment was fake, she knew she had been taken for a ride.
pubcol-w-0803214e730b73d5.vi_meaning_correction: lừa dối, lừa gạt ai đó

pubcol-w-d90f4a6b58bf0213.definition_en: to deceive or trick someone into believing something false
pubcol-w-d90f4a6b58bf0213.example_simple: Don't let his charm take you in.
pubcol-w-d90f4a6b58bf0213.example_complex: So many people were taken in by the scam that the losses ran into millions.
pubcol-w-d90f4a6b58bf0213.vi_meaning_correction: lừa gạt, đánh lừa ai đó

pubcol-w-b829e689193fa343.definition_en: to fail to appreciate someone or something because you are too used to them
pubcol-w-b829e689193fa343.example_simple: We often take our parents for granted.
pubcol-w-b829e689193fa343.example_complex: After living abroad, she realised how much she had taken the little comforts of home for granted.
pubcol-w-b829e689193fa343.vi_meaning_correction: không biết quý trọng, xem là điều hiển nhiên

pubcol-w-6f41f2bd463219bf.ipa: /teɪk ˈsʌmθɪŋ wɪð ə pɪntʃ əv sɔːlt/
pubcol-w-6f41f2bd463219bf.definition_en: to not fully believe something because it may not be true
collocations: take it with a pinch of salt
take his claims with a pinch of salt
should be taken with a pinch of salt
pubcol-w-6f41f2bd463219bf.example_simple: Take his advice with a pinch of salt.
pubcol-w-6f41f2bd463219bf.example_complex: Online reviews can be helpful, but the more extreme ones should be taken with a pinch of salt.
pubcol-w-6f41f2bd463219bf.vi_meaning_correction: không tin hoàn toàn, hoài nghi về điều gì đó

pubcol-w-d5703a34bbd7c9d5.definition_en: to consider something when making a decision or judgement
pubcol-w-d5703a34bbd7c9d5.example_simple: We must take the weather into account.
pubcol-w-d5703a34bbd7c9d5.example_complex: When setting the deadline, the manager took into account the team's current workload and available resources.
pubcol-w-d5703a34bbd7c9d5.vi_meaning_correction: cân nhắc, tính đến, xem xét điều gì đó

pubcol-w-4b2f2ef61224ab30.definition_en: to take charge or move into first position ahead of others
collocations: take the lead in the race
take the lead on a project
pubcol-w-4b2f2ef61224ab30.example_simple: She took the lead in the group project.
pubcol-w-4b2f2ef61224ab30.example_complex: The company took the lead in developing greener technology long before its rivals did.
pubcol-w-4b2f2ef61224ab30.vi_meaning_correction: dẫn đầu, giữ vai trò lãnh đạo

pubcol-w-445c4b59ea7937ce.definition_en: to make fun of someone in a teasing way (informal British English)
pubcol-w-445c4b59ea7937ce.example_simple: Stop taking the mickey out of my accent.
pubcol-w-445c4b59ea7937ce.example_complex: The comedian gently took the mickey out of the politicians in the front row.
pubcol-w-445c4b59ea7937ce.vi_meaning_correction: trêu chọc, chế giễu ai đó

pubcol-w-83b59521284032ce.definition_en: to make use of a chance to do something
collocations: take the opportunity while it lasts
pubcol-w-83b59521284032ce.example_simple: I'd like to take the opportunity to thank everyone.
pubcol-w-83b59521284032ce.example_complex: She took the opportunity of the quiet afternoon to catch up on the work she had fallen behind on.
pubcol-w-83b59521284032ce.vi_meaning_correction: nắm lấy cơ hội, tận dụng cơ hội

pubcol-w-9f38b039d0d707b7.definition_en: to run away or escape quickly, especially from danger
collocations: take to flight at the sight of
pubcol-w-9f38b039d0d707b7.example_simple: The birds took to flight when the dog barked.
pubcol-w-9f38b039d0d707b7.example_complex: At the first sound of gunfire, the crowd took to flight, scattering in every direction.

pubcol-w-96d68f75a24f6d5a.definition_en: to do something one after another rather than all at once
pubcol-w-96d68f75a24f6d5a.example_simple: The children take turns on the swing.
pubcol-w-96d68f75a24f6d5a.example_complex: To keep the project going overnight, the engineers took turns monitoring the servers in shifts.
